title: A section of a separated etale morphism is an open and closed immersion
statement: Let $\pi:P\to U$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] that is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $s:U\to P$ be a section, $\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}_U$. Then: (1) $s$ is etale (since $\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}_U$ is etale and $\pi$ is etale, in particular locally of finite type and unramified); (2) $s$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] (it is etale by (1), hence flat and locally of finite presentation, and a monomorphism, having the retraction $\pi$); (3) $s$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] (since $\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}_U$ is a closed immersion and $\pi$ is separated). Hence $s(U)$ is an open and closed subset of $P$, $s$ is an isomorphism of $U$ onto the open and closed subscheme $s(U)$, and $\pi|_{s(U)}:s(U)\to U$ is the inverse isomorphism.
